title: Diagnostic: The rules of the Layered Architecture should be followed
rationale: Traditional layering (application accessed only by incoming adapters) contradicts Ports and Adapters, where outgoing adapters implement application-level output ports; the hexagonal rules cover the intended dependency direction

title: Domain must not have dependencies on Infrastructure
rationale: Domain should not depend on infrastructure concerns (Dependency Inversion Principle)

title: Application Services must only use outbound ports (not infrastructure implementations)
rationale: Application services should only use outbound ports declared as interfaces (port.out), not infrastructure implementation details

title: Transaction boundaries belong to the application layer
rationale: Transactions are an application-layer concern - domain and incoming adapters must not manage them

title: The shared kernel's output-port markers must all be interfaces
rationale: port.out contains outbound port interfaces (Repository, OutputPort, DomainEventPublisher) shared across all bounded contexts. These must be interfaces to ensure the application layer remains framework-independent and follows the Dependency Inversion Principle. Implementations belong in infrastructure or adapter packages.

title: Domain must not access Application Services (Onion Architecture - Domain is innermost layer)
rationale: Domain is the innermost layer in onion architecture and should not depend on application services

title: The Domain Model should be framework independent and should not use 3rd party libraries when possible
rationale: Domain should be framework-independent (Dependency Inversion Principle)

title: Domain Models must not have Spring/JPA annotations
rationale: Domain models must be framework-independent (no Spring or JPA annotations)

title: Classes from the domain should not access port adapters
rationale: Domain should not depend on adapters (ports and adapters pattern)

title: Application Services should not access port adapters
rationale: Application services should only depend on domain and outbound ports, not adapters

title: Controllers and Resources must never access repositories directly
rationale: Controllers must go through use cases (input ports), never directly to repositories

title: Incoming Adapters must only use outbound ports (not infrastructure implementations)
rationale: Incoming adapters should only use outbound ports declared as interfaces (port.out), not infrastructure implementation details

title: Outgoing Adapters must only use outbound ports (not infrastructure implementations)
rationale: Outgoing adapters should only use outbound ports declared as interfaces (port.out), not infrastructure implementation details

title: Port adapters (incoming and outgoing) must not communicate directly with each other within the same context
rationale: Port adapters should communicate through application services, not directly (event consumers are the exception)

title: Incoming adapters must only access their own bounded context (except event consumers and Open Host Services)
rationale: Incoming adapters must only orchestrate use cases from their own bounded context - use domain events for cross-context integration

title: Classes named *Repository must reside in the outgoing adapter package
rationale: Repository implementations are secondary adapters (outgoing ports)

title: Output Ports in application.shared must extend OutputPort
rationale: Top-level interfaces in application.shared are output ports and must extend OutputPort to be part of the port hierarchy. Nested interfaces (e.g. IdentityProvider.Identity) are part of their enclosing port's contract, not ports themselves

title: Output ports must not reside in the domain layer
rationale: output ports (Repository, Store, OutputPort) are an application-layer concern and must live in application/shared/, not domain/

title: Incoming Adapters must depend on input port interfaces, not on use case classes
rationale: A driving adapter drives the application through its port. Injecting the concrete implementation instead couples the adapter to one realisation of the use case, defeats the Dependency Inversion Principle the port exists for, and makes the adapter untestable without the real use case and everything it depends on

title: Incoming Adapters must not depend on domain services
rationale: An incoming adapter translates external input, calls an input port and formats its result. Injecting or invoking a domain service bypasses the application boundary; the use case owns that collaboration and puts its outcome into the result. Outgoing adapters are outside this rule - repositories and other driven adapters may construct or reconstitute domain objects while implementing output ports

title: Aggregate Roots must implement AggregateRoot<T, ID>
rationale: Classes named *AggregateRoot must implement AggregateRoot interface (DDD pattern)

title: Aggregate Roots must not hold references to Repositories or other Output Ports
rationale: Aggregates are persistence-ignorant: repositories and services are passed as method parameters by the use case, never injected as fields

title: Aggregate Roots must not have fields with other Aggregate Root types
rationale: Vernon's Aggregate Design Rule #2: reference other Aggregates by identity to keep aggregate boundaries and transactional consistency intact

title: Entities must have an ID field
rationale: An Entity is defined by its identity, which is a value object implementing the Id marker

title: Entities must not be instantiated directly from outside the aggregate
rationale: Entities are created through their aggregate root so that the root can enforce its invariants

title: Domain model classes must not have public setter methods
rationale: Behavior-rich domain models change state through intention-revealing methods from the ubiquitous language, never through public setters

title: Entities must not have fields with Aggregate Root types
rationale: An entity inside an aggregate references other aggregates by identity only, otherwise the aggregate boundary leaks

title: Value Objects must not contain Aggregate Roots or Entities
rationale: A Value Object is defined by its attributes; holding an object with identity would give it a lifecycle it must not have

title: Value Object classes should be final (immutability)
rationale: Value objects should be immutable (final classes) - Vernon's DDD recommendation

title: Value Object fields must be final (deep immutability)
rationale: Records have implicitly final fields and enums are immutable by design; a hand-written value class must make every instance field final itself

title: Value Objects must not have setter methods
rationale: Value Objects are immutable; state changes produce a new instance instead of mutating

title: Value Objects must be records or immutable classes with attribute equality
rationale: A record grants attribute-based equality for free; a hand-written Value Object class must override equals and hashCode itself to compare by its attributes

title: Repository Interfaces should extend Repository Marker Interface
rationale: Repository interfaces should extend Repository marker interface

title: Repository interfaces must reside in the application layer's shared output-port package
rationale: Repository interfaces are output ports in the application layer (Hexagonal Architecture)

title: Repository Implementations must reside in adapter.outgoing package
rationale: Repository implementations are outgoing adapters in bounded contexts

title: Repositories must only exist for Aggregate Roots
rationale: A repository is the collection of one aggregate type; a repository for an entity would let callers bypass the root that guards the aggregate's invariants

title: Repository methods must not return non-root Entities
rationale: A caller receiving an Entity that is not an Aggregate Root could mutate part of an aggregate without passing its root, so the root's invariants would never run

title: Store interfaces must extend the Store marker, not Repository
rationale: Stores extend the Store marker; Repository is reserved for Aggregate Roots

title: Store interfaces must reside in the application layer's shared output-port package
rationale: Store interfaces are output ports in the application layer (Hexagonal Architecture)

title: Store implementations must reside in the adapter.outgoing package
rationale: Store implementations are outgoing adapters in bounded contexts

title: Store interfaces must not declare findById or save methods
rationale: findById/save are Repository semantics; a Store that has them is a Repository wearing the wrong name, and the stored object should then be an Aggregate Root

title: Enriched Domain Models must be Value Object records
rationale: Enriched domain models are immutable read projections and must be records implementing Value

title: Diagnostic: Display discovered bounded contexts
rationale: Making the discovered contexts visible shows which packages the strategic rules govern

title: Shared Kernel must not have dependencies on any bounded context
rationale: Shared Kernel must be context-independent — it is shared by all contexts and owned by none

title: Modules must not access each other in the application layer
rationale: An application layer talks to other modules through its own output ports, implemented by adapters - never directly. Selects structurally over every module that owns a DCA layer, declared as a bounded context or not: an undeclared module must not be able to escape isolation by staying off the context map

title: Modules must not access each other in the domain layer
rationale: A domain layer talks to its own module and the shared kernel, nothing else - not even another module's api/. Selects structurally over every module that owns a DCA layer, declared as a bounded context or not

title: Open Host Services must be published: in the api package or as an incoming adapter
rationale: An Open Host Service is the protocol a context publishes for other contexts - in-process as its api/ package, over the network as an incoming adapter (REST, gRPC, MCP). It belongs at the context boundary, never in the domain or application layer; the adapter's sub-package is irrelevant

title: Outgoing adapters accessing other modules must only use their published api/ and events/ packages
rationale: Cross-module communication goes through the target's published api/ (synchronous) and events/ (asynchronous) packages - DCA's in-process contract convention, package names rather than framework annotations - never through its domain, application, adapter or infrastructure packages. Selects structurally over every module that owns a DCA layer, declared as a bounded context or not

title: Integration Events must be in events or adapter outgoing event packages
rationale: Integration Events must be in events/ packages (published named interface) or adapter.outgoing.event/ packages

title: Integration Events should be immutable records
rationale: Integration Events must be immutable to ensure event integrity across contexts (Event Sourcing best practice)

title: Anti-Corruption Layer components must be in acl packages
rationale: Anti-Corruption Layer components must be in 'acl' packages for clear architectural intent (DDD Strategic Pattern)

title: Event Listeners consuming integration events should use Anti-Corruption Layer
rationale: Consumed integration events are translated into the consuming context's own language before they reach its domain — verified by code review, not statically

title: Upstream, ExternalUpstream, and Partnership may only be declared on bounded context packages
rationale: Context map declarations are reserved for bounded contexts — only a context can be downstream of, or partner with, another

title: ExternalUpstream declarations must be well-formed and unique per name and interaction
rationale: The identity of an @ExternalUpstream declaration is (name, interaction); internal contexts are declared with @Upstream instead

title: Distinct external system names must not collide after mermaid id normalization
rationale: The generated context map renders one node per normalized external system name — two spellings of the same system would silently merge into one node

title: Upstream declarations must reference an existing bounded context and never the declaring context itself
rationale: A dangling or self-referencing upstream edge describes a relationship that cannot exist

title: Upstream declarations must be unique per context and channel, and via must not be empty
rationale: The identity of an @Upstream declaration is (context, via); different translations per channel require separate annotations

title: Upstream declarations and Spring Modulith allowedDependencies must agree
rationale: Neither the context map nor the module boundary may know more than the other — an edge that exists only on one side is stale

title: Implemented Upstream declarations must be backed by an actual code dependency
rationale: A declared IMPLEMENTED edge without any real dependency is stale (or premature — then it is PLANNED) and would otherwise pass forever alongside an equally stale module boundary entry

title: Anti-Corruption Layer: upstream contract types must stay inside the matching adapter
rationale: The ACL sits where the dependency crosses the boundary — outgoing adapters for synchronous API calls, incoming adapters for consumed events — and translates the upstream contract into the context's own model there

title: Conformist: upstream contract types must never reach the domain layer
rationale: Conformism does not suspend domain purity — the domain layer stays free of foreign contract types

title: External system contract types must respect the declared translation and interaction
rationale: An external system's contract types are confined to the adapter where the exchange crosses the boundary (ACL) or at least kept out of the domain (Conformist)

title: Cross-context dependencies on published interfaces require an Upstream declaration
rationale: Every real dependency on a foreign api/ or events/ package is a context-map edge and must be declared as such

title: Partnership declarations must reference an existing bounded context, never themselves, and must be symmetric
rationale: A partnership is a mutual commitment — it exists only when both contexts declare it

title: Diagnostic: Display declared context map
rationale: Printing the declared edges makes the executable context map reviewable at a glance

title: Domain Events must implement DomainEvent Marker Interface and be records
rationale: Domain events should be immutable records implementing DomainEvent (named in past tense, e.g., ProductCreated, CartCleared)

title: Domain Events must reside in domain package
rationale: Domain events are part of the domain layer (named in past tense)

title: Domain Events should be immutable (final or records)
rationale: Domain events should be immutable (final classes or records)

title: Domain Events must not have Spring annotations
rationale: Domain events must be framework-independent POJOs

title: Integration Events must be annotated with IntegrationEventType
rationale: @IntegrationEventType(name, version) is the contract identity of every integration event — the serializer keys (name, version) to the class and stamps both onto the wire envelope

title: Integration Events must not have a version field
rationale: The schema version is a class property (@IntegrationEventType), never per-instance payload data — a version data field duplicates the annotation and can drift from it

title: Domain Events that are not Integration Events must not have a version field
rationale: Versioning is a contract concern of integration events — a purely internal domain event has no wire contract to version

title: Domain Events must have a timestamp field
rationale: An event records something that happened — without a timestamp the fact cannot be ordered, replayed or audited

title: Domain Services must implement DomainService Marker Interface and reside in domain.service
rationale: Domain services implement DomainService marker and reside in domain.service packages (named descriptively, e.g., PricingService, CartTotalCalculator)

title: Domain Services must reside in domain package
rationale: Domain services are part of the domain layer, not application layer

title: Domain Services must not have Spring annotations
rationale: Domain services should be framework-independent

title: Domain Services should be stateless (only final fields for dependencies)
rationale: Domain services should be stateless (only final fields for dependencies)

title: Factories should implement Factory Marker Interface
rationale: Classes implementing Factory marker should have 'Factory' in their name

title: Factories must reside in domain package
rationale: Factories are part of the domain layer (complex aggregate creation logic)

title: Factories must not have Spring annotations
rationale: Factories should be framework-independent

title: Factories should be stateless (only final fields for dependencies)
rationale: Factories should be stateless (only final fields for dependencies)

title: Specifications must end with 'Specification'
rationale: Specification implementations are part of the domain layer

title: Specifications must not have Spring annotations
rationale: Specifications should be framework-independent value objects

title: Base InputPort interface must be in the building-blocks port in package
rationale: Base InputPort interface defines the generic contract for all use cases (Hexagonal Architecture)

title: Use Case Commands must end with 'Command' and reside in application package
rationale: Use case commands should be in application layer (CQRS pattern)

title: Use Case Queries must end with 'Query' and reside in application package
rationale: Use case queries should be in application layer (CQRS pattern)

title: Use Case Commands should be immutable (final or records)
rationale: Use case commands should be immutable (value objects)

title: Use Case Queries should be immutable (final or records)
rationale: Use case queries should be immutable (value objects)

title: Use Case Result Models must end with 'Result' and reside in application package
rationale: Use case result models should be in application layer. Domain Value Objects with 'Result' in name are allowed in domain layer.

title: Use Case Result Models should be immutable (final or records)
rationale: Use case result models should be immutable (value objects)

title: HTTP Response Models must end with 'Response' and reside in adapter incoming package
rationale: HTTP response models should be in adapter incoming layer

title: Use cases that save an aggregate must publish its domain events
rationale: A saved aggregate must not keep its events: unpublished, they are lost, and stored on the instance they may later be published out of context. Publishing belongs after the save, in the use case that owns the unit of work - even when the action raised no event

title: DTOs must not be used in the Domain Layer
rationale: Domain layer should not depend on DTOs (presentation concerns) - Dependency Inversion Principle

title: DTOs must not be used in the Application Layer
rationale: Application layer should use Command/Query/Response models, not presentation DTOs (Clean Architecture)

title: Use cases that publish domain events must have a transaction boundary
rationale: Integration events are relayed after commit (@TransactionalEventListener, @ApplicationModuleListener) and their publication is registered in the publishing transaction. Without an active transaction the after-commit listeners are skipped silently and nothing is registered: the use case succeeds, the other contexts never hear of it. The use case that publishes owns the boundary - either declarative transaction metadata (@Transactional on the class or the executing method) or an explicit TransactionBoundary.inTransaction(...) around save and publish

title: Declaratively transactional use cases must not call remote-capable output ports
rationale: A @Transactional use case holds a database connection for its whole run. Calling an output port that may leave the process (another context's API, a payment provider, a mail gateway) inside it blocks that connection for the remote round trip; under load the pool runs dry, and a rollback cannot undo the remote effect. Only transactional resources belong inside the boundary: Repository, Store, DomainEventPublisher, IntegrationEventPublisher. Everything else is called before the transaction - draw the boundary by hand with TransactionBoundary.inTransaction(...) - or after it, as a reaction to an integration event

title: Use case packages within a module must use one consistent depth (flat or grouped by feature)
rationale: A use case package sits either directly below the application package (application.<usecase>) or one level deeper inside a feature (application.<feature>.<usecase>). A feature is an optional, domain-named group of related use cases - a navigation boundary inside one bounded context, not a layer, module or aggregate owner. Mixing both forms in one module makes it unclear whether a package is a feature, a use case or a leftover; nesting deeper than a feature hides the use case. The rule checks legibility only: it does not infer bounded contexts, feature semantics or aggregate ownership. application.shared holds the context-wide output ports and is not a use case package

title: Use Case Result Models must not expose aggregate roots or entities
rationale: A result is the use case's answer, not a handle on the model: identity and behaviour stay behind the port; values, enriched models and read models may cross. Checked transitively through nested records, part records anywhere in the application layer (application.shared included) and generic type arguments (List<T>, Optional<T>, Map<K,V>)

title: Application layer InputPort implementations must end with 'UseCase'
rationale: InputPort implementations (use cases) should follow consistent naming conventions (Hexagonal Architecture)

title: Use case classes must be annotated with @Service
rationale: Use case classes must be Spring-managed beans

title: InputPort interfaces must end with 'InputPort'
rationale: Input port interfaces should follow consistent naming conventions (Hexagonal Architecture)

title: Repository Interfaces must end with 'Repository'
rationale: Repository interfaces should follow consistent naming conventions (DDD pattern)

title: Controller classes must end with 'Controller'
rationale: @Controller annotated classes should follow naming conventions

title: REST Controllers must end with 'Resource' (REST best practice)
rationale: @RestController annotated classes should end with 'Resource' following RESTful naming conventions

title: DTOs must reside in the adapter layer, not in domain or application
rationale: DTOs are adapter concerns (presentation or external API) - not in domain or application

title: Converters must reside in the adapter layer
rationale: Converters/Mappers translate between layers and should be in adapters

title: No technical bucket packages - package by domain concept
rationale: Packages are named after domain concepts from the ubiquitous language, not technical patterns

title: Domain classes must not use technical suffixes (Manager, Helper, Util, Impl)
rationale: Domain names come from the ubiquitous language - name services by their specialty, not by technical role

title: ViewModels must reside in adapter.incoming.web packages
rationale: ViewModels are presentation concerns and must reside in incoming web adapter packages

title: Domain Packages must not have cyclic dependencies
rationale: Domain model packages should have clear boundaries and no cycles (Acyclic Dependencies Principle)

title: Application Layer must not have cyclic dependencies
rationale: Application services should have clear boundaries and no cycles

title: Outgoing Adapter Packages must not have cyclic dependencies
rationale: Outgoing adapters should have clear boundaries and no cycles

title: Incoming Adapter Packages must not have cyclic dependencies
rationale: Incoming adapters should have clear boundaries and no cycles

title: Feature and use case packages within a module's application layer must not have cyclic dependencies
rationale: The packages directly below a module's application package are its features (application.<feature>.<usecase>) or, in a flat layout, its use cases (application.<usecase>). A feature is an optional, domain-named group of related use cases; it may depend on another feature in one direction, but a cycle between two of them means the grouping does not carry its weight - the shared concept belongs in application.shared, in the domain, or in one of the two. application.shared is the context-wide port package and is not a slice. The rule does not infer bounded contexts or aggregate ownership from the packages it slices
